# Is My Copy of In Other Words (In altre parole) a First Edition?

Alfred A. Knopf, 2016 · Hardcover (trade)

Last reviewed 4 July 2026 · CC BY 4.0

Quick answer

A first edition of In Other Words (In altre parole) by Jhumpa Lahiri (Alfred A. Knopf, 2016) is identified by: Dual-language edition with the Italian text on the left-hand pages and Ann Goldstein's English translation on the facing right-hand pages (ISBN 978-1-101-87555-1). The Italian original In altre parole (Guanda, 2015) is the true first; the Knopf bilingual edition of 2016 is the first US and first English-language appearance, in Ann Goldstein's translation.

Checklist — a true first has these:

- Dual-language edition with the Italian text on the left-hand pages and Ann Goldstein's English translation on the facing right-hand pages (ISBN 978-1-101-87555-1) P-014473
- The first US printing states 'First American Edition' on the copyright page with a number line ending in 1, and is issued in cloth in a pictorial dust jacket retaining its printed flap price on a correct first-issue copy P-014474
- Publisher imprint reads Alfred A. Knopf
- Not a book-club edition (see below)

The first US printing states 'First American Edition' on the copyright page with a number line ending in 1, and is issued in cloth in a pictorial dust jacket retaining its printed flap price on a correct first-issue copy. The Italian original In altre parole (Guanda, 2015) is the true first; the Knopf bilingual edition of 2016 is the first US and first English-language appearance, in Ann Goldstein's translation. No notable book-club edition. The Bloomsbury UK edition is a separate English printing distinct from the Knopf first American edition.

url_citation.title: Living Outside of Language with Jhumpa Lahiri's 'In Other Words' » PopMatters
url_citation.content:
By

 Diane Leach

/ 30 March 2016 

In Other Words (In Altre Parole)

Jhumph Lahiri

Knopf

February 2016

...

In Other Words is printed in an unusual format: the left side of the text is in Italian, the right in English. Monolingual English readers quickly grow accustomed to reading only the right side of the book. Having little Italian, I don’t know whether bilinguals will find the pagination maddening or enjoyable.
